questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Facade pattern?

options.text: Provide a unified, higher-level interface that makes a complex subsystem easier to use
Convert one class's interface into another
Add responsibilities to an object dynamically
Clone objects from a prototype

questions.explanation: Facade simplifies a subsystem behind one interface. Converting an interface = Adapter; adding responsibilities = Decorator; cloning = Prototype.

questions.prompt: Does a Facade prevent callers from using the subsystem directly?

options.text: No — it offers an easy path but leaves the subsystem reachable for advanced needs
Yes — the subsystem becomes completely inaccessible
Yes — it deletes the subsystem classes
Only if the subsystem is a singleton

questions.explanation: A facade simplifies the common case without hiding or forbidding direct subsystem access for edge cases.

questions.prompt: How does Facade differ from Adapter?

options.text: Facade wraps many classes behind a new simpler interface; Adapter converts one object's interface to a specific expected one
They are identical
Facade changes an interface; Adapter simplifies a subsystem
Facade controls access; Adapter adds behavior

questions.explanation: Facade = simplify many; Adapter = convert one interface into a specific expected interface.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk of a Facade over time?

options.text: It can swell into a god object that accumulates too many responsibilities
It forces two threads to collide
It always makes the subsystem slower
It prevents dependency injection

questions.explanation: If every feature is bolted on, the facade relocates the complexity it was meant to hide — the god-object anti-pattern.

questions.prompt: A key benefit of Facade is that it reduces ____ between client code and a complex subsystem.
questions.explanation: Clients depend on the single facade instead of many subsystem internals, lowering coupling.

questions.prompt: In the order example, what does placeOrder() encode so clients don't have to?

options.text: The correct sequence: reserve inventory, then charge payment, then schedule shipping
The single global instance of the order
How to deep-copy the order
How to convert the order to another interface

questions.explanation: The facade captures the workflow and ordering across subsystems so each caller doesn't repeat it.
